A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CorrSteer research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization and identifiable appendix omissions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark, ablation, transferability, and feature-analysis results, including Gemma/LLaMA experiments and GPT-2 steering on EMGSD.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated steering comparators and multi-seed Gemma results in Table 1.

M1.justification: Pearson selection from generated-token SAE activations, positive-outcome mean coefficients, residual-stream steering, and single/all/pruned-layer variants remain unchanged. CorrSteer-1 becomes CorrSteer-S. The dedicated pooling subsection reorganizes existing choices, including mean-pooled coefficients for GSM8K.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, both BBQ conditions, SimpleQA, HarmBench, and XSTest, plus EMGSD classification steering. The new comparator results use retained task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated adaptations of CAA, SPARE (MI), and DSG (Fisher) across seven Gemma tasks; these were cited but not benchmarked in v1. Fine-tuning and the existing appendix comparators remain. The new methods have no reported GSM8K results.

E3.justification: v2 Section 5.1 introduces controlled adaptations for the new comparisons: MI/Fisher replace feature selection while sharing generation-time activations and positive-mean coefficients, whereas CAA uses correct/incorrect activation differences. Existing splits and training budgets remain unchanged. Shot settings are newly disclosed rather than established protocol changes.

E4.justification: The controlled MI/Fisher substitutions add evidence about the feature-selection criterion. Existing pooling, negative-feature, raw/decoder, and cross-task analyses in Tables 5–8 and the sample-scaling plot are retained. Conversely, v2 reduces Gemma SimpleQA/XSTest feature-inspection evidence through omitted list entries and the missing XSTest coefficient plot.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without run counts. v2 Table 1 introduces means and standard deviations across five seeds, or three for GSM8K, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. This does not establish v1's run count. Despite Appendix A.1's statement about all results, retained LLaMA and ablation tables still show point estimates.

E6.justification: Gemma Table 1 is substantially revised and expanded. CorrSteer-A's MMLU result changes from 56.32 to 55.48±0.59, HarmBench from 67.50 to 73.75±8.84, and GSM8K from 54.44 to 40.34±24.43. These replace point estimates with multi-seed summaries. New comparator scores are added; retained LLaMA and Tables 5–9 scores match.

T1.justification: v1 Section 2.1's formal SAE encoder/decoder definitions and reconstruction-plus-sparsity objective, Equations 1–3, are omitted. CorrSteer's correlation, coefficient, residual-steering, and SER mathematics remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central automated generation-time steering contribution is retained. The abstract narrows 'avoiding' spurious correlations to 'reducing' them and revises headline MMLU/HarmBench gains from 4.1%/22.9% to 3.3%/27.2%. The headline HarmBench sample count changes from 4,000 to 108.

C2.justification: v1 Section 6.3 qualifies the circuit interpretation as lacking explicit interaction and causality analysis; v2 Section 5.5 asserts that interventions establish causal relationships. v2 also recommends approximately 4,000 samples for stability, adds small-sample variance limitations, explicitly distinguishes increased refusal from fine-grained safety, and reinterprets EMGSD mitigation scores as increased fairness.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and explicit shot settings, while retaining the principal implementation hyperparameters. However, Appendix A.8.1 drops 22 Gemma SimpleQA and seven XSTest feature-description/coefficient/correlation entries. Remaining XSTest entries appear beneath the SimpleQA heading, weakening the feature documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tan et al. (2024) on steering reliability and changes PaCE's characterization from orthogonal steering directions to oblique projection. The overall prior-work positioning remains similar, with added discussion explaining the adapted CAA, SPARE, and DSG comparisons.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and reorganized: Background becomes Related Work, pooling receives a method subsection, Results and Discussion are merged, and Conclusion and Limitations are combined. Future Work and Acknowledgments are removed. The title and variant terminology also change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column format, adds the Figure 1 system diagram, transposes and expands Table 1, and moves LLaMA tables into the appendix. Appendix figures gain numbering, several displays are removed, and Table 9 gains score-direction labels. Most retained plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added steering comparisons and multi-seed Gemma results improve scrutiny of performance and reliability, exposing instability hidden by v1's point estimates. The gain is limited by inconsistent uncertainty coverage, text–table contradictions such as the GSM8K fine-tuning comparison in Section 5.1, stronger causal assertions without new causal analysis, and the missing or misassigned SimpleQA/XSTest appendix entries.
